mcqs.q: A linear polynomial is of degree =
mcqs.why: A linear polynomial has highest power 1, as given in the Review Exercise. Step 1: Linear means degree 1, so the answer is 1.

mcqs.q: A quadratic polynomial is of degree =
mcqs.why: A quadratic polynomial has highest power 2, as given in the Review Exercise. Step 1: Quadratic means degree 2, so the answer is 2.

mcqs.q: A cubic polynomial is of degree =
mcqs.why: A cubic polynomial has highest power 3, as given in the Review Exercise. Step 1: Cubic means degree 3, so the answer is 3.

mcqs.q: Factorization of (x + 3)^2 - 4 is
mcqs.why: Formula: u^2 - v^2 = (u - v)(u + v), with u = x + 3 and v = 2. Step 1: (x + 3)^2 - 4 = (x + 3 - 2)(x + 3 + 2). Step 2: = (x + 1)(x + 5), which matches the book keyed answer.

mcqs.q: Factorization of x^4 - 16 is
mcqs.why: Formula: u^2 - v^2 = (u - v)(u + v) applied twice. Step 1: x^4 - 16 = (x^2 - 4)(x^2 + 4). Step 2: x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2). Step 3: = (x - 2)(x + 2)(x^2 + 4), the book keyed answer.

mcqs.q: Factorization of x^3 - y^3 is =
mcqs.why: Formula: u^3 - v^3 = (u - v)(u^2 + uv + v^2), with u = x and v = y. Step 1: x^3 - y^3 = (x - y)(x^2 + xy + y^2), which matches the book keyed answer.

mcqs.q: Factorization of a^4 - 1 is =
mcqs.why: Formula: u^2 - v^2 = (u - v)(u + v) applied twice. Step 1: a^4 - 1 = (a^2 - 1)(a^2 + 1). Step 2: a^2 - 1 = (a - 1)(a + 1). Step 3: = (a - 1)(a + 1)(a^2 + 1), the book keyed answer.

mcqs.q: If a polynomial P(x) is divided by the polynomial x - a, where a is any constant, then P(a) is
mcqs.why: Remainder theorem: on dividing P(x) by (x - a), the remainder is P(a). Step 1: Substitute x = a. Step 2: The value P(a) is the remainder, which matches the book keyed answer.

mcqs.q: If x - a is a factor of P(x), then P(a) =
mcqs.why: Factor theorem: x - a is a factor of P(x) exactly when P(a) = 0. Step 1: If (x - a) divides P(x) with no remainder, the remainder P(a) must be 0, matching the book keyed answer.

mcqs.q: Factorization of x^2 - 9 is
mcqs.why: Formula: u^2 - v^2 = (u - v)(u + v), with u = x and v = 3. Step 1: x^2 - 9 = x^2 - 3^2. Step 2: = (x - 3)(x + 3), which matches the Review fill-in answer.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.1 — H.C.F. by Factorization
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 3.1 of Unit 3 — Algebraic Manipulation — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q1 Find H.C.F by factorization: abxy, a^2bc

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Factorize: abxy = a.b.x.y; a^2bc = a.a.b.c. Common factors: a x b.
H.C.F = ab.
(Answer: ab.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q2 Find H.C.F: 6pqr, 15qrs

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
6pqr = 2.3.p.q.r; 15qrs = 3.5.q.r.s. Common factors: 3 x q x r.
H.C.F = 3qr.
(Answer: 3qr.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q3 Find H.C.F: 8xy^2z^3, 12x^2y^2z^2

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Common coefficient: H.C.F(8, 12) = 4. Common variables with lowest powers: x^1, y^2, z^2.
H.C.F = 4xy^2z^2.
(Answer: 4xy^2z^2.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q4 Find H.C.F: 14a^2bc, 21ab^2

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
H.C.F(14, 21) = 7; common variables: a^1, b^1 (c is not common).
H.C.F = 7ab.
(Answer: 7ab.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q5 Find H.C.F: 3x^5y^2, 12x^2y^4, 15x^3y^2

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
H.C.F(3, 12, 15) = 3; lowest powers: x^2, y^2.
H.C.F = 3x^2y^2.
(Answer: 3x^2y^2.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q6 Find H.C.F: 4abc^3, 8a^3bc, 6ab^3c

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
H.C.F(4, 8, 6) = 2; lowest powers: a^1, b^1, c^1.
H.C.F = 2abc.
(Answer: 2abc.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q7 Find H.C.F: x^3 + 64, x^2 - 16

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Step 1: x^3 + 64 = (x + 4)(x^2 - 4x + 16).
Step 2: x^2 - 16 = (x - 4)(x + 4).
Step 3: Common factor: (x + 4).
H.C.F = x + 4.
(Answer: x + 4.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q8 Find H.C.F: x^2 - y^2, x^4 - y^4, x^6 - y^6

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Step 1: x^4 - y^4 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^2 + y^2); x^6 - y^6 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^4 + x^2y^2 + y^4).
Step 2: The factor (x^2 - y^2) is common to all three.
H.C.F = x^2 - y^2.
(Answer: x^2 - y^2.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q9 Find H.C.F: t^2 - 9, (t + 3)^2, t^2 + t - 6

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Step 1: t^2 - 9 = (t - 3)(t + 3); t^2 + t - 6 = (t + 3)(t - 2).
Step 2: Common factor of all three: (t + 3).
H.C.F = t + 3.
(Answer: t + 3.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q10 Find H.C.F: x^2 - x - 2, x^2 + x - 6, x^2 - 3x + 2

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Step 1: x^2 - x - 2 = (x - 2)(x + 1); x^2 + x - 6 = (x + 3)(x - 2); x^2 - 3x + 2 = (x - 1)(x - 2).
Step 2: Common factor: (x - 2).
H.C.F = x - 2.
(Answer: x - 2.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q11 Find H.C.F: 1 - x^2, x^3 + 1, 1 - x - 2x^2

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Step 1: 1 - x^2 = (1 - x)(1 + x); x^3 + 1 = (x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1); 1 - x - 2x^2 = (1 + x)(1 - 2x).
Step 2: Common factor: (x + 1).
H.C.F = x + 1.
(Answer: x + 1.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q12 Find H.C.F: x^3 - 8, x^2 - 7x + 10

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Step 1: x^3 - 8 = (x - 2)(x^2 + 2x + 4); x^2 - 7x + 10 = (x - 2)(x - 5).
Step 2: Common factor: (x - 2).
H.C.F = x - 2.
(Answer: x - 2.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q13 Find H.C.F: x^2 + 3x + 2, x^2 + 4x + 3, x^2 + 5x + 4

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Step 1: (x + 1)(x + 2); (x + 1)(x + 3); (x + 1)(x + 4).
Step 2: Common factor: (x + 1).
H.C.F = x + 1.
(Answer: x + 1.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q14 Find H.C.F: x^4 + x^3 - 6x^2, x^4 - 9x^2, x^3 + x^2 - 6x

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
Step 1: x^4 + x^3 - 6x^2 = x^2(x + 3)(x - 2); x^4 - 9x^2 = x^2(x - 3)(x + 3); x^3 + x^2 - 6x = x(x + 3)(x - 2).
Step 2: Common factors: x x (x + 3).
H.C.F = x(x + 3) = x^2 + 3x.
(Answer: x(x + 3) = x^2 + 3x.)

Exercise 3.1

Q. Q15 Find H.C.F: 35a^2c^3b, 45a^3cb^2, 30ac^2b^3

Method: factorize each expression and take the product of the common factors (lowest powers).
H.C.F(35, 45, 30) = 5; lowest powers: a^1, b^1, c^1.
H.C.F = 5abc.
(Answer: 5abc.)

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of abxy and a^2bc?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize and take common factors with lowest powers. abxy = a.b.x.y and a^2bc = a.a.b.c. Common factors are a and b, so H.C.F = a x b = ab.

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of 6pqr and 15qrs?
mcqs.why: Method: H.C.F = H.C.F of coefficients times common variables with lowest powers. 6pqr = 2.3.p.q.r and 15qrs = 3.5.q.r.s. Common factors are 3, q and r, so H.C.F = 3qr.

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of 8xy^2z^3 and 12x^2y^2z^2?
mcqs.why: Method: take H.C.F of coefficients and lowest powers of common variables. H.C.F(8, 12) = 4. Lowest powers are x^1, y^2 and z^2. So H.C.F = 4 x x x y^2 x z^2 = 4xy^2z^2.

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of 14a^2bc and 21ab^2?
mcqs.why: Method: H.C.F = product of common factors with lowest powers. H.C.F(14, 21) = 7. Common variables are a^1 and b^1; c is not common. So H.C.F = 7 x a x b = 7ab.

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of 3x^5y^2, 12x^2y^4 and 15x^3y^2?
mcqs.why: Method: take H.C.F of all coefficients and lowest powers. H.C.F(3, 12, 15) = 3. Lowest powers are x^2 and y^2. So H.C.F = 3 x x^2 x y^2 = 3x^2y^2.

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of x^3 + 64 and x^2 - 16?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize, then take the common factor. x^3 + 64 = (x + 4)(x^2 - 4x + 16) and x^2 - 16 = (x - 4)(x + 4). The common factor is (x + 4), so H.C.F = x + 4.

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of t^2 - 9, (t + 3)^2 and t^2 + t - 6?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize each expression and take the factor common to all. t^2 - 9 = (t - 3)(t + 3) and t^2 + t - 6 = (t + 3)(t - 2). The factor (t + 3) appears in all three, so H.C.F = t + 3.

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of x^2 - x - 2, x^2 + x - 6 and x^2 - 3x + 2?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize each quadratic. x^2 - x - 2 = (x - 2)(x + 1); x^2 + x - 6 = (x + 3)(x - 2); x^2 - 3x + 2 = (x - 1)(x - 2). The common factor is (x - 2), so H.C.F = x - 2.

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of 35a^2c^3b, 45a^3cb^2 and 30ac^2b^3?
mcqs.why: Method: H.C.F = H.C.F of coefficients times lowest powers of common variables. H.C.F(35, 45, 30) = 5. Lowest powers are a^1, b^1 and c^1. So H.C.F = 5 x a x b x c = 5abc.

mcqs.q: What is the H.C.F of x^2 - y^2, x^4 - y^4 and x^6 - y^6?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize using difference of squares. x^4 - y^4 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^2 + y^2) and x^6 - y^6 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^4 + x^2y^2 + y^4). The factor (x^2 - y^2) is common to all three, so H.C.F = x^2 - y^2.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.2 — H.C.F. by the Division Method
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 3.2 of Unit 3 — Algebraic Manipulation — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q1 Find H.C.F by division method: x^4 + x^2 + 1, x^4 + x^3 + x + 1

Step 1: Divide x^4 + x^3 + x + 1 by x^4 + x^2 + 1: quotient 1, remainder x^3 - x^2 + x = x(x^2 - x + 1).
Step 2: Divide x^4 + x^2 + 1 by (x^2 - x + 1): quotient x^2 + x + 1, remainder 0.
Step 3: The last non-zero divisor is the H.C.F.
(Answer: x^2 - x + 1.)

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q2 Find H.C.F by division method: 6x^3 + 7x^2 - 9x + 2, 8x^4 + 6x^3 - 15x^2 + 9x - 2

Step 1: Divide the 4th-degree polynomial by the 3rd-degree one and continue the Euclidean process (divide, take remainder, repeat).
Step 2: The successive remainders reduce to a constant multiple of 2x^2 + 3x - 2, which divides both exactly (check: 6x^3 + 7x^2 - 9x + 2 = (2x^2 + 3x - 2)(3x - 1) + 0... verified by factorization (2x - 1)(x + 2) divides both).
Step 3: H.C.F = 2x^2 + 3x - 2.
(Answer: 2x^2 + 3x - 2.)

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q3 Find H.C.F by division method: 4x^3 + 2x^2 - 6x, 4x^3 - 8x + 4

Step 1: Divide 4x^3 - 8x + 4 by 4x^3 + 2x^2 - 6x (after removing common monomial factors 2x and 4): work with x^2(2x + 1) - 3x... using the division chain the last divisor is a constant multiple of (x - 1).
Step 2: Check: 4x^3 + 2x^2 - 6x at x = 1 gives 0; 4x^3 - 8x + 4 at x = 1 gives 0.
Step 3: H.C.F = x - 1 (the H.C.F is unaffected by constant multiples, as the book notes).
(Answer: x - 1 (up to a constant factor 2).)

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q4 Find H.C.F by division method: x^3 + 7x^2 + 12x, x^3 - 2x^2 - 15x

Step 1: Both have the factor x; divide x^2 + 7x + 12 by x^2 - 2x - 15: remainder 9x + 27 = 9(x + 3).
Step 2: Divide x^2 - 2x - 15 by (x + 3): quotient x - 5, remainder 0.
Step 3: H.C.F = x(x + 3) = x^2 + 3x.
(Answer: x(x + 3) = x^2 + 3x.)

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q5 Find H.C.F by division method: x^3 - x^2 - x + 1, x^4 - 2x^3 + 2x - 1

Step 1: Divide x^4 - 2x^3 + 2x - 1 by x^3 - x^2 - x + 1: quotient (x - 1), remainder 0.
Step 2: The division is exact, so the divisor itself is the H.C.F.
H.C.F = x^3 - x^2 - x + 1.
(Answer: x^3 - x^2 - x + 1.)

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q6 Find H.C.F by division method: x^3 - x^2 - x - 2, x^3 + 3x^2 - 6x - 8

Step 1: Subtract/divide: (x^3 + 3x^2 - 6x - 8) - (x^3 - x^2 - x - 2) = 4x^2 - 5x - 6; continuing the division chain gives the last divisor (x - 2).
Step 2: Check: both polynomials vanish at x = 2 (8 - 4 - 2 - 2 = 0; 8 + 12 - 12 - 8 = 0).
H.C.F = x - 2.
(Answer: x - 2.)

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q7 Find H.C.F by division method: x^2 + 3x - 4, x^3 - 2x^2 - 2x + 3

Step 1: Divide x^3 - 2x^2 - 2x + 3 by x^2 + 3x - 4: quotient (x - 5), remainder 17x - 17 = 17(x - 1).
Step 2: Divide x^2 + 3x - 4 by (x - 1): quotient x + 4, remainder 0.
H.C.F = x - 1.
(Answer: x - 1.)

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q8 Find H.C.F by division method: 3x^3 - 14x^2 + 9x + 10, 15x^3 - 34x^2 + 21x - 10

Step 1: 5 x (first) = 15x^3 - 70x^2 + 45x + 50; subtract the second: -36x^2 + 24x + 60 = -12(3x^2 - 2x - 5); continuing the chain, the last divisor is (3x - 5).
Step 2: Check: both vanish at x = 5/3.
H.C.F = 3x - 5.
(Answer: 3x - 5.)

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q9 Find H.C.F by division method: 2x^4 + x^3 + 4x + 2, 6x^3 + 5x^2 + x, 2x^4 + 3x^3 + x^2 + 2x + 1

Step 1: Apply the division process to the first two, then divide the third by the result.
Step 2: The common last divisor of all three is (2x + 1) (each polynomial vanishes at x = -1/2).
H.C.F = 2x + 1.
(Answer: 2x + 1.)

Exercise 3.2

Q. Q10 Find H.C.F by division method: x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 3, x^3 - 7x + 6, x^3 + 2x^2 - 2x + 3

Step 1: (x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 3) - (x^3 - 7x + 6) = x^2 + 2x - 3 = (x + 3)(x - 1); continuing the chain with the third polynomial, the last common divisor is (x + 3).
Step 2: Check: all three vanish at x = -3 (-27 + 9 + 15 + 3 = 0; -27 + 21 + 6 = 0; -27 + 18 + 6 + 3 = 0).
H.C.F = x + 3.
(Answer: x + 3.)

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of x^4 + x^2 + 1 and x^4 + x^3 + x + 1?
mcqs.why: Division method: divide x^4 + x^3 + x + 1 by x^4 + x^2 + 1; quotient 1, remainder x^3 - x^2 + x = x(x^2 - x + 1). Next divide x^4 + x^2 + 1 by (x^2 - x + 1); quotient x^2 + x + 1, remainder 0. Last non-zero divisor is the H.C.F = x^2 - x + 1.

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of 6x^3 + 7x^2 - 9x + 2 and 8x^4 + 6x^3 - 15x^2 + 9x - 2?
mcqs.why: Division method: apply the Euclidean process, dividing and taking remainders in turn. The remainders reduce to a constant multiple of 2x^2 + 3x - 2, which divides both exactly, since 6x^3 + 7x^2 - 9x + 2 = (2x^2 + 3x - 2)(3x - 1). So H.C.F = 2x^2 + 3x - 2.

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of 4x^3 + 2x^2 - 6x and 4x^3 - 8x + 4?
mcqs.why: Division method: continue the division chain; the last divisor is a constant multiple of (x - 1). Check: at x = 1, 4x^3 + 2x^2 - 6x = 4 + 2 - 6 = 0 and 4x^3 - 8x + 4 = 4 - 8 + 4 = 0. So H.C.F = x - 1, up to a constant factor.

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of x^3 + 7x^2 + 12x and x^3 - 2x^2 - 15x?
mcqs.why: Division method: both have factor x. Divide x^2 + 7x + 12 by x^2 - 2x - 15; remainder is 9x + 27 = 9(x + 3). Divide x^2 - 2x - 15 by (x + 3); quotient x - 5, remainder 0. Restoring factor x gives H.C.F = x(x + 3) = x^2 + 3x.

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of x^3 - x^2 - x + 1 and x^4 - 2x^3 + 2x - 1?
mcqs.why: Division method: divide x^4 - 2x^3 + 2x - 1 by x^3 - x^2 - x + 1. The quotient is (x - 1) and the remainder is 0. The division is exact, so the divisor itself is the H.C.F = x^3 - x^2 - x + 1.

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of x^3 - x^2 - x - 2 and x^3 + 3x^2 - 6x - 8?
mcqs.why: Division method: subtract to get (x^3 + 3x^2 - 6x - 8) - (x^3 - x^2 - x - 2) = 4x^2 - 5x - 6, and continuing the chain gives last divisor (x - 2). Check: both vanish at x = 2, since 8 - 4 - 2 - 2 = 0 and 8 + 12 - 12 - 8 = 0. So H.C.F = x - 2.

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of x^2 + 3x - 4 and x^3 - 2x^2 - 2x + 3?
mcqs.why: Division method: divide x^3 - 2x^2 - 2x + 3 by x^2 + 3x - 4; quotient (x - 5), remainder 17x - 17 = 17(x - 1). Next divide x^2 + 3x - 4 by (x - 1); quotient x + 4, remainder 0. So H.C.F = x - 1.

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of 3x^3 - 14x^2 + 9x + 10 and 15x^3 - 34x^2 + 21x - 10?
mcqs.why: Division method: 5 times the first polynomial minus the second gives -36x^2 + 24x + 60 = -12(3x^2 - 2x - 5); continuing the chain, the last divisor is (3x - 5). Check: both polynomials vanish at x = 5/3. So H.C.F = 3x - 5.

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of 2x^4 + x^3 + 4x + 2, 6x^3 + 5x^2 + x and 2x^4 + 3x^3 + x^2 + 2x + 1?
mcqs.why: Division method: apply the process to the first two polynomials, then divide the third by the result. The common last divisor of all three is (2x + 1). Check: each polynomial vanishes at x = -1/2. So H.C.F = 2x + 1.

mcqs.q: By the division method, what is the H.C.F of x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 3, x^3 - 7x + 6 and x^3 + 2x^2 - 2x + 3?
mcqs.why: Division method: (x^3 + x^2 - 5x + 3) - (x^3 - 7x + 6) = x^2 + 2x - 3 = (x + 3)(x - 1); continuing with the third polynomial, the last common divisor is (x + 3). Check: all three vanish at x = -3. So H.C.F = x + 3.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.3 — L.C.M. by Factorization
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 3.3 of Unit 3 — Algebraic Manipulation — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q1 Find L.C.M by factorization: 21a^4x^3y, 35a^2x^4y, 28a^3xy^4

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
L.C.M of coefficients (21, 35, 28) = 420; highest powers: a^4, x^4, y^4.
(Answer: 420a^4x^4y^4.)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q2 Find L.C.M: 3a^4b^2c^3, 5a^2b^3c^5

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
L.C.M of coefficients = 15; highest powers: a^4, b^3, c^5.
(Answer: 15a^4b^3c^5.)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q3 Find L.C.M: 2ab, 3ab, 4ca

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
L.C.M of coefficients (2, 3, 4) = 12; variables a, b, c each to power 1.
(Answer: 12abc.)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q4 Find L.C.M: x^2yz, xy^2z, xyz^2

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Highest powers: x^2, y^2, z^2.
(Answer: x^2y^2z^2.)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q5 Find L.C.M: p^3q - pq^3, p^5q^2 - p^2q^5

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: p^3q - pq^3 = pq(p - q)(p + q); p^5q^2 - p^2q^5 = p^2q^2(p - q)(p^2 + pq + q^2).
Step 2: Take every factor with its highest power.
(Answer: p^2q^2(p - q)(p + q)(p^2 + pq + q^2).)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q6 Find L.C.M: x^3 + 64, x^2 - 16

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: x^3 + 64 = (x + 4)(x^2 - 4x + 16); x^2 - 16 = (x - 4)(x + 4).
Step 2: L.C.M = common factor (x + 4) x uncommon factors (x - 4)(x^2 - 4x + 16).
(Answer: (x - 4)(x + 4)(x^2 - 4x + 16).)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q7 Find L.C.M: x^2 - x - 2, x^2 + x - 6, x^2 - 3x + 2

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: (x - 2)(x + 1); (x + 3)(x - 2); (x - 1)(x - 2).
Step 2: L.C.M = (x - 2)(x + 1)(x + 3)(x - 1).
(Answer: (x - 2)(x - 1)(x + 1)(x + 3).)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q8 Find L.C.M: y^2 - 9, (y + 3)^2, y^2 + y - 6

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: y^2 - 9 = (y - 3)(y + 3); y^2 + y - 6 = (y + 3)(y - 2).
Step 2: Highest powers: (y + 3)^2, (y - 3), (y - 2).
(Answer: (y - 3)(y - 2)(y + 3)^2.)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q9 Find L.C.M: 1 - y^2, y^3 + 1, 1 - y - 2y^2

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: 1 - y^2 = (1 - y)(1 + y); y^3 + 1 = (y + 1)(y^2 - y + 1); 1 - y - 2y^2 = (1 + y)(1 - 2y).
Step 2: L.C.M = (y + 1)(y - 1)(2y - 1)(y^2 - y + 1) (up to sign).
(Answer: (y - 1)(y + 1)(2y - 1)(y^2 - y + 1).)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q10 Find L.C.M: x^2 - y^2, x^4 - y^4, x^6 - y^6

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: x^4 - y^4 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^2 + y^2); x^6 - y^6 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^2 + xy + y^2)(x^2 - xy + y^2).
Step 2: Take all distinct factors.
(Answer: (x - y)(x + y)(x^2 + y^2)(x^2 - xy + y^2)(x^2 + xy + y^2).)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q11 Find L.C.M: x^3 + 1, x^4 + x^2 + 1, (x^2 + x + 1)^2

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: x^3 + 1 = (x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1); x^4 + x^2 + 1 = (x^2 + x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1).
Step 2: Highest powers: (x + 1), (x^2 - x + 1), (x^2 + x + 1)^2.
(Answer: (x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1)(x^2 + x + 1)^2.)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q12 Find L.C.M: x^3 + y^3, x^4 - y^4, x^6 + y^6

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: x^3 + y^3 = (x + y)(x^2 - xy + y^2); x^4 - y^4 = (x - y)(x + y)(x^2 + y^2); x^6 + y^6 = (x^2 + y^2)(x^4 - x^2y^2 + y^4).
Step 2: Take all distinct factors.
(Answer: (x - y)(x + y)(x^2 + y^2)(x^2 - xy + y^2)(x^4 - x^2y^2 + y^4).)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q13 Find L.C.M: 2x^2 + 5x + 3, x^2 + 2x + 1, 2x^2 + 9x + 9

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: 2x^2 + 5x + 3 = (2x + 3)(x + 1); x^2 + 2x + 1 = (x + 1)^2; 2x^2 + 9x + 9 = (2x + 3)(x + 3).
Step 2: Highest powers of all factors.
(Answer: (x + 1)^2(x + 3)(2x + 3).)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q14 Find L.C.M: x^4 + x^3 - 6x^2, x^4 - 9x^2, x^3 + x^2 - 6x

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: x^2(x + 3)(x - 2); x^2(x - 3)(x + 3); x(x + 3)(x - 2).
Step 2: L.C.M = x^2 (x - 3)(x + 3)(x - 2).
(Answer: x^2(x - 3)(x - 2)(x + 3).)

Exercise 3.3

Q. Q15 Find L.C.M: x^2 + 4xy + 4y^2, x^2 + 3xy + 2y^2, x^2 + 2xy + y^2

Method: L.C.M = product of common factors x product of uncommon factors (each factor with its highest power).
Step 1: (x + 2y)^2; (x + y)(x + 2y); (x + y)^2.
Step 2: L.C.M = (x + y)^2 (x + 2y)^2.
(Answer: (x + y)^2(x + 2y)^2.)

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of 21a^4x^3y, 35a^2x^4y and 28a^3xy^4?
mcqs.why: Method: L.C.M = common factors times uncommon factors, each with its highest power. L.C.M of coefficients (21, 35, 28) = 420. Highest powers are a^4, x^4 and y^4. So L.C.M = 420 x a^4 x x^4 x y^4 = 420a^4x^4y^4.

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of 3a^4b^2c^3 and 5a^2b^3c^5?
mcqs.why: Method: take L.C.M of coefficients and highest power of each variable. L.C.M of coefficients (3, 5) = 15. Highest powers are a^4, b^3 and c^5. So L.C.M = 15 x a^4 x b^3 x c^5 = 15a^4b^3c^5.

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of 2ab, 3ab and 4ca?
mcqs.why: Method: L.C.M = product of all distinct factors with highest powers. L.C.M of coefficients (2, 3, 4) = 12. Variables a, b and c each occur to power 1. So L.C.M = 12 x a x b x c = 12abc.

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of x^2yz, xy^2z and xyz^2?
mcqs.why: Method: for L.C.M take each variable with its highest power. Highest powers are x^2, y^2 and z^2. So L.C.M = x^2 x y^2 x z^2 = x^2y^2z^2.

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of x^3 + 64 and x^2 - 16?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize, then take every factor with its highest power. x^3 + 64 = (x + 4)(x^2 - 4x + 16) and x^2 - 16 = (x - 4)(x + 4). L.C.M = common factor (x + 4) times uncommon factors (x - 4)(x^2 - 4x + 16) = (x - 4)(x + 4)(x^2 - 4x + 16).

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of x^2 - x - 2, x^2 + x - 6 and x^2 - 3x + 2?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize each quadratic. x^2 - x - 2 = (x - 2)(x + 1); x^2 + x - 6 = (x + 3)(x - 2); x^2 - 3x + 2 = (x - 1)(x - 2). Take each distinct factor once: L.C.M = (x - 2)(x + 1)(x + 3)(x - 1).

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of y^2 - 9, (y + 3)^2 and y^2 + y - 6?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize: y^2 - 9 = (y - 3)(y + 3) and y^2 + y - 6 = (y + 3)(y - 2). Highest powers are (y + 3)^2, (y - 3) and (y - 2). So L.C.M = (y - 3)(y - 2)(y + 3)^2.

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of x^2 - y^2, x^4 - y^4 and x^6 - y^6?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize: x^4 - y^4 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^2 + y^2) and x^6 - y^6 = (x^2 - y^2)(x^2 + xy + y^2)(x^2 - xy + y^2). Take all distinct factors: L.C.M = (x - y)(x + y)(x^2 + y^2)(x^2 - xy + y^2)(x^2 + xy + y^2).

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of 2x^2 + 5x + 3, x^2 + 2x + 1 and 2x^2 + 9x + 9?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize: 2x^2 + 5x + 3 = (2x + 3)(x + 1); x^2 + 2x + 1 = (x + 1)^2; 2x^2 + 9x + 9 = (2x + 3)(x + 3). Take highest powers of all factors: L.C.M = (x + 1)^2(x + 3)(2x + 3).

mcqs.q: What is the L.C.M of x^2 + 4xy + 4y^2, x^2 + 3xy + 2y^2 and x^2 + 2xy + y^2?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize: x^2 + 4xy + 4y^2 = (x + 2y)^2; x^2 + 3xy + 2y^2 = (x + y)(x + 2y); x^2 + 2xy + y^2 = (x + y)^2. Highest powers give L.C.M = (x + y)^2(x + 2y)^2.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.5 — Simplifying Algebraic Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 3.5 of Unit 3 — Algebraic Manipulation — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q1 Simplify: 1/a + 2/(a + 1) - 3/(a + 2)

Step 1: L.C.M of denominators = a(a + 1)(a + 2).
Step 2: Numerator: (a + 1)(a + 2) + 2a(a + 2) - 3a(a + 1) = (a^2 + 3a + 2) + (2a^2 + 4a) - (3a^2 + 3a) = 4a + 2.
Step 3: = (4a + 2)/(a(a + 1)(a + 2)) = 2(2a + 1)/(a(a + 1)(a + 2)).
(Answer: 2(2a + 1)/(a(a + 1)(a + 2)).)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q2 Simplify: 2a/(x - 2a) - (x - a)/(x^2 - 5ax + 6a^2) + 2/(x - 3a)

Step 1: x^2 - 5ax + 6a^2 = (x - 2a)(x - 3a); L.C.M = (x - 2a)(x - 3a).
Step 2: Numerator: 2a(x - 3a) - (x - a) + 2(x - 2a) = (2ax - 6a^2) - x + a + 2x - 4a = 2ax + x - 6a^2 - 3a.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: (x - 3a)(2a + 1) = 2ax + x - 6a^2 - 3a. Yes.
Step 4: Cancel (x - 3a): = (2a + 1)/(x - 2a).
(Answer: (2a + 1)/(x - 2a).)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q3 Simplify: 1/(a^2 + 1) - a^4/(a^2 + 1) + a^6/(a^2 - 1) - 1/(a^2 - 1)

Step 1: Group by denominators: (1 - a^4)/(a^2 + 1) + (a^6 - 1)/(a^2 - 1).
Step 2: (1 - a^4)/(a^2 + 1) = -(a^2 - 1)(a^2 + 1)/(a^2 + 1) = -(a^2 - 1) = 1 - a^2.
Step 3: (a^6 - 1)/(a^2 - 1) = a^4 + a^2 + 1.
Step 4: Sum: (1 - a^2) + (a^4 + a^2 + 1) = a^4 + 2.
(Answer: a^4 + 2.)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q4 Simplify: 1/(x^2 + x + 1) - 1/(x^2 - x + 1) + (2x + 1)/(x^4 + x^2 + 1)

Step 1: x^4 + x^2 + 1 = (x^2 + x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1); combine the first two fractions over it: numerator (x^2 - x + 1) - (x^2 + x + 1) = -2x.
Step 2: So the expression = (-2x + 2x + 1)/(x^4 + x^2 + 1) = 1/(x^4 + x^2 + 1).
(Answer: 1/(x^4 + x^2 + 1).)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q5 Simplify: a^2(b - c)/((a + b)(a + c)) - b^2(c - a)/((b + c)(b + a)) + c^2(a - b)/((c + a)(c + b))

Step 1: L.C.M of denominators = (a + b)(b + c)(c + a). Multiply the first term by (b + c), the second by (c + a), the third by (a + b).
Step 2: Expanding the combined numerator, the terms cancel in pairs and it reduces to 2b^2(a^2 - c^2) = 2b^2(a - c)(a + c).
Step 3: Cancel (a + c): = 2b^2(a - c)/((a + b)(b + c)). (Verified by symbolic simplification.)
(Answer: 2b^2(a - c)/((a + b)(b + c)).)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q6 Simplify: 1/(x - 1) + 1/(x + 1) - (x + 2)/(x^2 + x + 1) - (x - 2)/(x^2 - x + 1)

Step 1: 1/(x - 1) + 1/(x + 1) = 2x/(x^2 - 1).
Step 2: Note (x^2 - 1)(x^2 + x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1) = x^6 - 1; combining all fractions over x^6 - 1, the numerator reduces to 6x^3.
Step 3: = 6x^3/(x^6 - 1). (Verified by symbolic simplification.)
(Answer: 6x^3/(x^6 - 1).)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q7 Simplify: (a^2 + ab + b^2)/(a + b) + (a^2 - ab + b^2)/(a - b)

Step 1: L.C.M = (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2.
Step 2: Numerator: (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) + (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2) = (a^3 - b^3) + (a^3 + b^3) = 2a^3.
Step 3: = 2a^3/(a^2 - b^2).
(Answer: 2a^3/(a^2 - b^2).)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q8 Simplify: ((x^4 - y^4)/(x^2 - 2xy + y^2)) x ((x - y)/(x(x + y))) / ((x^2 + y^2)/x)

Step 1: Factor: x^4 - y^4 = (x - y)(x + y)(x^2 + y^2); x^2 - 2xy + y^2 = (x - y)^2.
Step 2: Division by (x^2 + y^2)/x means multiply by x/(x^2 + y^2).
Step 3: Product = [(x - y)(x + y)(x^2 + y^2)/(x - y)^2] x [(x - y)/(x(x + y))] x [x/(x^2 + y^2)] = 1 after cancelling (x - y), (x + y), (x^2 + y^2) and x.
(Answer: 1.)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q9 Simplify: ((x^2 - 1)/(x^2 + x - 2)) x ((x^3 + 8)/(x^4 + 4x^2 + 16)) / ((x^2 + x)/(x^3 + 2x^2 + 4x))

Step 1: Factor: x^2 - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1); x^2 + x - 2 = (x + 2)(x - 1); x^3 + 8 = (x + 2)(x^2 - 2x + 4); x^4 + 4x^2 + 16 = (x^2 + 2x + 4)(x^2 - 2x + 4); x^2 + x = x(x + 1); x^3 + 2x^2 + 4x = x(x^2 + 2x + 4).
Step 2: Turn the division into multiplication by the reciprocal and cancel (x - 1), (x + 2), (x^2 - 2x + 4), (x^2 + 2x + 4), x and (x + 1).
Step 3: = 1.
(Answer: 1.)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q10 Simplify: ((a^3 + 64b^3)/(a^2 + 20ab + 64b^2)) / ((a^2 - 4ab + 16b^2)/(a^2 + 4ab + 16b^2)) x ((a^2 + 12ab - 64b^2)/(a^3 - 64b^3))

Step 1: Factor: a^3 + 64b^3 = (a + 4b)(a^2 - 4ab + 16b^2); a^2 + 20ab + 64b^2 = (a + 4b)(a + 16b); a^2 + 12ab - 64b^2 = (a + 16b)(a - 4b); a^3 - 64b^3 = (a - 4b)(a^2 + 4ab + 16b^2).
Step 2: Convert the division to multiplication by the reciprocal; every factor cancels in pairs: (a + 4b), (a^2 - 4ab + 16b^2), (a + 16b), (a - 4b), (a^2 + 4ab + 16b^2).
Step 3: = 1.
(Answer: 1.)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q11 Simplify: (a/((a + b)^2 - 2ab)) x ((a^4 - b^4)/((a + b)^3 - 3ab(a + b))) / (((a + b)^2 - 4ab)/((a + b)^2 - 3ab))

Step 1: Simplify the compound denominators: (a + b)^2 - 2ab = a^2 + b^2; (a + b)^3 - 3ab(a + b) = a^3 + b^3; (a + b)^2 - 4ab = (a - b)^2; (a + b)^2 - 3ab = a^2 - ab + b^2.
Step 2: The expression becomes [a/(a^2 + b^2)] x [(a^4 - b^4)/(a^3 + b^3)] x [(a^2 - ab + b^2)/(a - b)^2].
Step 3: a^4 - b^4 = (a - b)(a + b)(a^2 + b^2) and a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2); cancelling (a^2 + b^2), (a + b), (a^2 - ab + b^2) and one (a - b) leaves a/(a - b).
(Answer: a/(a - b).)

Exercise 3.5

Q. Q12 Simplify: ((a^2 - 1)/(a^2 - a - 2)) / ((a^2 + 5a + 6)/(a^2 - 5a + 6)) / ((a^2 - 4a + 3)/(a^2 + 4a + 3))

Step 1: Factor all parts: a^2 - 1 = (a - 1)(a + 1); a^2 - a - 2 = (a - 2)(a + 1); a^2 + 5a + 6 = (a + 2)(a + 3); a^2 - 5a + 6 = (a - 2)(a - 3); a^2 - 4a + 3 = (a - 1)(a - 3); a^2 + 4a + 3 = (a + 1)(a + 3).
Step 2: Convert both divisions to multiplications by reciprocals and cancel (a - 1), (a + 1), (a - 2), (a - 3), (a + 3).
Step 3: = (a + 1)/(a + 2).
(Answer: (a + 1)/(a + 2).)

mcqs.why: Method: use L.C.M of denominators a(a + 1)(a + 2). Numerator = (a + 1)(a + 2) + 2a(a + 2) - 3a(a + 1) = (a^2 + 3a + 2) + (2a^2 + 4a) - (3a^2 + 3a) = 4a + 2. So result = (4a + 2)/(a(a + 1)(a + 2)) = 2(2a + 1)/(a(a + 1)(a + 2)).

Method: factor x^2 - 5ax + 6a^2 = (x - 2a)(x - 3a), so L.C.M = (x - 2a)(x - 3a). Numerator = 2a(x - 3a) - (x - a) + 2(x - 2a) = 2ax + x - 6a^2 - 3a = (x - 3a)(2a + 1). Cancel (x - 3a) to get (2a + 1)/(x - 2a).

Method: group by denominators: (1 - a^4)/(a^2 + 1) + (a^6 - 1)/(a^2 - 1). First part = -(a^2 - 1)(a^2 + 1)/(a^2 + 1) = 1 - a^2. Second part = a^4 + a^2 + 1. Sum = (1 - a^2) + (a^4 + a^2 + 1) = a^4 + 2.

Method: use x^4 + x^2 + 1 = (x^2 + x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1). Combine the first two fractions over it: numerator = (x^2 - x + 1) - (x^2 + x + 1) = -2x. Add the third term: (-2x + 2x + 1)/(x^4 + x^2 + 1) = 1/(x^4 + x^2 + 1).

Method: first, 1/(x - 1) + 1/(x + 1) = 2x/(x^2 - 1). Since (x^2 - 1)(x^2 + x + 1)(x^2 - x + 1) = x^6 - 1, combine all fractions over x^6 - 1; the numerator reduces to 6x^3. So result = 6x^3/(x^6 - 1).

mcqs.q: Simplify: (a^2 + ab + b^2)/(a + b) + (a^2 - ab + b^2)/(a - b)
mcqs.why: Method: L.C.M = (a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2. Numerator = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) + (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2) = (a^3 - b^3) + (a^3 + b^3) = 2a^3. So result = 2a^3/(a^2 - b^2).

mcqs.q: Simplify the compound fraction with factors (x^4 - y^4)/(x^2 - 2xy + y^2) times (x - y)/(x(x + y)) divided by (x^2 + y^2)/x
mcqs.why: Method: factor x^4 - y^4 = (x - y)(x + y)(x^2 + y^2) and x^2 - 2xy + y^2 = (x - y)^2. Dividing by (x^2 + y^2)/x means multiplying by x/(x^2 + y^2). Cancelling (x - y), (x + y), (x^2 + y^2) and x leaves 1.

mcqs.q: Simplify: (a/((a + b)^2 - 2ab)) times ((a^4 - b^4)/((a + b)^3 - 3ab(a + b))) divided by (((a + b)^2 - 4ab)/((a + b)^2 - 3ab))
mcqs.why: Method: (a + b)^2 - 2ab = a^2 + b^2; (a + b)^3 - 3ab(a + b) = a^3 + b^3; (a + b)^2 - 4ab = (a - b)^2; (a + b)^2 - 3ab = a^2 - ab + b^2. Using a^4 - b^4 = (a - b)(a + b)(a^2 + b^2) and a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2), cancelling leaves a/(a - b).

mcqs.q: Simplify: ((a^2 - 1)/(a^2 - a - 2)) divided by ((a^2 + 5a + 6)/(a^2 - 5a + 6)) divided by ((a^2 - 4a + 3)/(a^2 + 4a + 3))
mcqs.why: Method: factor all parts: a^2 - 1 = (a - 1)(a + 1); a^2 - a - 2 = (a - 2)(a + 1); a^2 + 5a + 6 = (a + 2)(a + 3); a^2 - 5a + 6 = (a - 2)(a - 3); a^2 - 4a + 3 = (a - 1)(a - 3); a^2 + 4a + 3 = (a + 1)(a + 3). Convert divisions to reciprocals and cancel (a - 1), (a + 1), (a - 2), (a - 3), (a + 3) to get (a + 1)/(a + 2).

Method: L.C.M of denominators = (a + b)(b + c)(c + a). Multiply the first term by (b + c), the second by (c + a) and the third by (a + b). The combined numerator reduces to 2b^2(a^2 - c^2) = 2b^2(a - c)(a + c). Cancel (a + c) to get 2b^2(a - c)/((a + b)(b + c)).

lessons.title: Exercise 3.6 — Square Root of Algebraic Expressions
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 3.6 of Unit 3 — Algebraic Manipulation — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q1 Find the square root: 16x^2 + 24xy + 9y^2

= (4x)^2 + 2(4x)(3y) + (3y)^2 = (4x + 3y)^2.
Square root: +/-(4x + 3y).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q2 Find the square root: (x^2 - 7x + 12)(x^2 - 9x + 20)(x^2 - 8x + 15)

Step 1: x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x - 3)(x - 4); x^2 - 9x + 20 = (x - 4)(x - 5); x^2 - 8x + 15 = (x - 3)(x - 5).
Step 2: Product = (x - 3)^2 (x - 4)^2 (x - 5)^2.
Square root: +/-(x - 3)(x - 4)(x - 5).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q3 Find the square root: (x^2 + 8x + 7)(2x^2 - x - 3)(2x^2 + 11x - 21)

Step 1: x^2 + 8x + 7 = (x + 1)(x + 7); 2x^2 - x - 3 = (2x - 3)(x + 1); 2x^2 + 11x - 21 = (2x - 3)(x + 7).
Step 2: Product = (x + 1)^2 (x + 7)^2 (2x - 3)^2.
Square root: +/- (x + 1)(x + 7)(2x - 3).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q4 Find the square root: x(x + 2)(x + 4)(x + 6) + 16

Step 1: Pair x(x + 6) = x^2 + 6x and (x + 2)(x + 4) = x^2 + 6x + 8. Put z = x^2 + 6x: product + 16 = z(z + 8) + 16 = z^2 + 8z + 16 = (z + 4)^2.
Step 2: = (x^2 + 6x + 4)^2.
Square root: +/-(x^2 + 6x + 4).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q5 Find the square root: (2x + 1)(2x + 3)(2x + 5)(2x + 7) + 16

Step 1: Pair (2x + 1)(2x + 7) = 4x^2 + 16x + 7 and (2x + 3)(2x + 5) = 4x^2 + 16x + 15. Put z = 4x^2 + 16x: product + 16 = (z + 7)(z + 15) + 16 = z^2 + 22z + 121 = (z + 11)^2.
Step 2: = (4x^2 + 16x + 11)^2.
Square root: +/-(4x^2 + 16x + 11).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q6 Find the square root: (x^2 + 1/x^2) - 10(x + 1/x) + 27, x not 0

Step 1: Put u = x + 1/x; then x^2 + 1/x^2 = u^2 - 2.
Step 2: Expression = u^2 - 2 - 10u + 27 = u^2 - 10u + 25 = (u - 5)^2.
Square root: +/-(x + 1/x - 5).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q7 Find the square root: (t - 1/t)^2 - 4(t + 1/t) + 8, t not 0

Step 1: Put v = t + 1/t; then (t - 1/t)^2 = v^2 - 4.
Step 2: Expression = v^2 - 4 - 4v + 8 = v^2 - 4v + 4 = (v - 2)^2.
Square root: +/-(t + 1/t - 2).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q8 Find the square root: (x^2 + 1/x^2)^2 - 4(x + 1/x)^2 + 12, x not 0

Step 1: Put u = x + 1/x; x^2 + 1/x^2 = u^2 - 2, so (x^2 + 1/x^2)^2 = (u^2 - 2)^2 = u^4 - 4u^2 + 4.
Step 2: Expression = u^4 - 4u^2 + 4 - 4u^2 + 12 = u^4 - 8u^2 + 16 = (u^2 - 4)^2.
Step 3: u^2 - 4 = (x + 1/x)^2 - 4 = x^2 - 2 + 1/x^2.
Square root: +/-(x^2 - 2 + 1/x^2).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q9 Find the square root: 4x^4 + 12x^3 + 25x^2 + 24x + 16

By the division method (or by inspection): (2x^2 + 3x + 4)^2 = 4x^4 + 12x^3 + (9 + 16)x^2 + 24x + 16 = the given expression.
Square root: +/-(2x^2 + 3x + 4).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q10 Find the square root: 9x^2/(4y^2) - 3x/(2y) - 7/4 + 2y/(3x) + 4x^2/(9y^2), (x, y not 0)

Step 1: Put s = 3x/(2y) and t = 2y/(3x), so st = 1 and the expression is s^2 - s - 7/4 + t + t^2.
Step 2: (s - t - 1/2)^2 = s^2 + t^2 + 1/4 - 2st - s + t = s^2 + t^2 - s + t - 7/4 (since 2st = 2). This equals the given expression.
Square root: +/- (3x/(2y) - 2y/(3x) - 1/2).

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q11 For what value of x is x^4 + 4x^2 + x + 8/x^2 + 4/x^4 a complete square, where x not 0

Step 1: (x^2 + 2 + 2/x^2)^2 = x^4 + 4x^2 + 8 + 8/x^2 + 4/x^4.
Step 2: The given expression differs from this square by (x - 8).
Step 3: It is a complete square exactly when x - 8 = 0, i.e. x = 8.
Square root: x = 8.

Exercise 3.6

Q. Q12 If x^4 + lx^3 + mx^2 + 12x + 9 is a complete square then find the values of l and m

Step 1: The square root must be of the form (x^2 + px + 3); its square is x^4 + 2p x^3 + (p^2 + 6) x^2 + 6p x + 9.
Step 2: Compare the x term: 6p = 12, so p = 2.
Step 3: l = 2p = 4; m = p^2 + 6 = 4 + 6 = 10.
Square root: l = 4, m = 10.

mcqs.q: What is the square root of 16x^2 + 24xy + 9y^2?
mcqs.why: Method: recognize a perfect square, a^2 + 2ab + b^2 = (a + b)^2. Here 16x^2 + 24xy + 9y^2 = (4x)^2 + 2(4x)(3y) + (3y)^2 = (4x + 3y)^2. Taking the square root gives +/-(4x + 3y).

mcqs.q: What is the square root of (x^2 - 7x + 12)(x^2 - 9x + 20)(x^2 - 8x + 15)?
mcqs.why: Method: factorize each quadratic, then take the square root factor by factor. x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x - 3)(x - 4); x^2 - 9x + 20 = (x - 4)(x - 5); x^2 - 8x + 15 = (x - 3)(x - 5). Product = (x - 3)^2(x - 4)^2(x - 5)^2, so square root = +/-(x - 3)(x - 4)(x - 5).

mcqs.q: What is the square root of x(x + 2)(x + 4)(x + 6) + 16?
mcqs.why: Method: pair factors with the same sum. x(x + 6) = x^2 + 6x and (x + 2)(x + 4) = x^2 + 6x + 8. Put z = x^2 + 6x: product + 16 = z(z + 8) + 16 = z^2 + 8z + 16 = (z + 4)^2 = (x^2 + 6x + 4)^2. Square root = +/-(x^2 + 6x + 4).

mcqs.q: What is the square root of (2x + 1)(2x + 3)(2x + 5)(2x + 7) + 16?
What is the square root of (x^2 + 1/x^2) - 10(x + 1/x) + 27, where x is not 0?
mcqs.why: Method: substitute u = x + 1/x, so x^2 + 1/x^2 = u^2 - 2. Expression = u^2 - 2 - 10u + 27 = u^2 - 10u + 25 = (u - 5)^2. Substituting back, square root = +/-(x + 1/x - 5).

mcqs.q: What is the square root of (t - 1/t)^2 - 4(t + 1/t) + 8, where t is not 0?
mcqs.why: Method: put v = t + 1/t, so (t - 1/t)^2 = v^2 - 4. Expression = v^2 - 4 - 4v + 8 = v^2 - 4v + 4 = (v - 2)^2. Substituting back, square root = +/-(t + 1/t - 2).

mcqs.q: What is the square root of 4x^4 + 12x^3 + 25x^2 + 24x + 16?
mcqs.why: Method: check the square (2x^2 + 3x + 4)^2 = 4x^4 + 12x^3 + (9 + 16)x^2 + 24x + 16 = 4x^4 + 12x^3 + 25x^2 + 24x + 16, which equals the given expression. So square root = +/-(2x^2 + 3x + 4).

mcqs.q: What is the square root of (x^2 + 8x + 7)(2x^2 - x - 3)(2x^2 + 11x - 21)?
For what value of x is x^4 + 4x^2 + x + 8/x^2 + 4/x^4 a complete square, where x is not 0?
mcqs.why: Method: compare with (x^2 + 2 + 2/x^2)^2 = x^4 + 4x^2 + 8 + 8/x^2 + 4/x^4. The given expression differs from this square by (x - 8). It is a complete square exactly when x - 8 = 0, so x = 8.

mcqs.q: If x^4 + lx^3 + mx^2 + 12x + 9 is a complete square, what are the values of l and m?
mcqs.why: Method: the square root must be (x^2 + px + 3); its square is x^4 + 2p x^3 + (p^2 + 6)x^2 + 6p x + 9. Compare the x term: 6p = 12, so p = 2. Then l = 2p = 4 and m = p^2 + 6 = 4 + 6 = 10.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 3 — Unit 3 Review — Algebraic Manipulation
lessons.notes_html:
Review Exercise 3 of Unit 3 — Algebraic Manipulation — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Review Exercise 3

Q1 (Product of two expressions)/(L.C.M) = ?

(a) H.C.F   (b) L.C.M   (c) L.C.M x H.C.F   (d) L.C.M + H.C.F

Correct answer: H.C.F

Review Exercise 3

Q2 The number of methods to find L.C.M are:

(a) 0   (b) 1   (c) 2   (d) 3

Correct answer: 2

Review Exercise 3

Q3 The number of methods to find the H.C.F are:

(a) 4   (b) 1   (c) 2   (d) 3

Correct answer: 2

Review Exercise 3

Q4 H.C.F of 12pq, 8p^2q is:

(a) 4pq   (b) 4p^2q^2   (c) 4pq^2   (d) 4p^2q

Correct answer: 4pq

Review Exercise 3

Q5 H.C.F of 2x^2 + 3x + 1, 2x^2 - x - 1 is:

(a) 2x - 1   (b) 2x + 1   (c) x + 1   (d) x - 1

Correct answer: 2x + 1

Review Exercise 3

Q6 H.C.F of 6pqr, 15qrs is:

(a) 3qr   (b) 3pqr   (c) 3pqrs   (d) 15pqrs

Correct answer: 3qr

Review Exercise 3

Q7 L.C.M of 12p^3q^2, 8p^2q is:

(a) 24pq^2   (b) 24p^3q   (c) 24p^3q^2   (d) 12p^2q

Correct answer: 24p^3q^2

Review Exercise 3

Q8 Product of two expressions =

(a) H.C.F   (b) L.C.M   (c) H.C.F x L.C.M   (d) H.C.F + L.C.M

Correct answer: H.C.F x L.C.M

Review Exercise 3

Q9 (Product of two expressions)/(H.C.F) =

(a) L.C.M   (b) H.C.F   (c) 0   (d) L.C.M x H.C.F

Correct answer: L.C.M

Review Exercise 3

Q10 (L.C.M x H.C.F)/(First Expression) =

(a) second expression   (b) 1   (c) H.C.F   (d) L.C.M

Review Exercise 3

Q. Review Exercise 3, Part II - Fill in the blanks

Note: In this copy of the textbook, the printed page carrying Part II (fill in the blanks) of Review Exercise 3 (book page 84, top) is defective - the text is washed out and only the blank lines are visible, so the questions cannot be read. The blanks are therefore NOT solved here; nothing has been invented. The MCQ part (Part I) above is complete from the legible page 83.

mcqs.q: (Product of two expressions)/(L.C.M) = ?
mcqs.why: Use the relation Product of two expressions = H.C.F x L.C.M. Dividing both sides by L.C.M gives (Product)/(L.C.M) = H.C.F. So the required value is H.C.F.

mcqs.q: The number of methods to find L.C.M are:
mcqs.why: From the unit, L.C.M can be found by the methods taught in this chapter, and the book keys the number of methods as 2. Factorization is the method used throughout Exercise 3.3.

mcqs.q: The number of methods to find the H.C.F are:
mcqs.why: From the unit, H.C.F is found by factorization in Exercise 3.1 and by the division method in Exercise 3.2. That makes 2 methods in total, as keyed in the book.

mcqs.q: H.C.F of 12pq, 8p^2q is:
mcqs.why: Method: H.C.F = H.C.F of coefficients times lowest powers of common variables. H.C.F(12, 8) = 4. Lowest powers are p^1 and q^1. So H.C.F = 4 x p x q = 4pq.
Method: factorize both quadratics. 2x^2 + 3x + 1 = (2x + 1)(x + 1) and 2x^2 - x - 1 = (2x + 1)(x - 1). The common factor is (2x + 1), so H.C.F = 2x + 1.

mcqs.q: H.C.F of 6pqr, 15qrs is:
mcqs.why: Method: factorize: 6pqr = 2.3.p.q.r and 15qrs = 3.5.q.r.s. Common factors are 3, q and r. So H.C.F = 3 x q x r = 3qr, matching Exercise 3.1 Q2.

mcqs.q: L.C.M of 12p^3q^2, 8p^2q is:
mcqs.why: Method: L.C.M = L.C.M of coefficients times highest powers. L.C.M(12, 8) = 24. Highest powers are p^3 and q^2. So L.C.M = 24 x p^3 x q^2 = 24p^3q^2.

mcqs.q: Product of two expressions =
mcqs.why: The fundamental relation of this unit is Product of two expressions = H.C.F x L.C.M. This is the identity used in the review questions to find any one quantity from the other two.

mcqs.q: (Product of two expressions)/(H.C.F) =
mcqs.why: Use Product of two expressions = H.C.F x L.C.M. Dividing both sides by H.C.F gives (Product)/(H.C.F) = L.C.M. So the required value is L.C.M.

mcqs.q: (L.C.M x H.C.F)/(First Expression) =
mcqs.why: Use L.C.M x H.C.F = First Expression x Second Expression. Dividing both sides by the First Expression gives (L.C.M x H.C.F)/(First Expression) = second expression.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.1 — Linear Equations in One Variable
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 4.1 of Unit 4 — Linear Equations and Inequalities — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q1(i) Solve: 3x + 20 = 44

Step 1: Transpose 20: 3x = 44 - 20 = 24.
Step 2: Divide by 3: x = 8.
Check: 3(8) + 20 = 44. Correct.
(Answer: x = 8.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q1(ii) Solve: 4x/5 - 3x/4 = 4

Step 1: L.C.M of 5, 4 is 20; multiply both sides by 20: 16x - 15x = 80.
Step 2: x = 80.
Check: 4(80)/5 - 3(80)/4 = 64 - 60 = 4. Correct.
(Answer: x = 80.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q1(iii) Solve: 3x + 3(x + 1) = 69

Step 1: Open the bracket: 3x + 3x + 3 = 69, so 6x + 3 = 69.
Step 2: 6x = 66, x = 11.
Check: 33 + 3(12) = 69. Correct.
(Answer: x = 11.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q1(iv) Solve: (90 - 9x) + 27 = 90 + 9

Step 1: Simplify: 117 - 9x = 99.
Step 2: -9x = 99 - 117 = -18, so x = 2.
Check: (90 - 18) + 27 = 99 = 90 + 9. Correct.
(Answer: x = 2.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q2 Solve: 3(x + 3) = 14 + x

Step 1: 3x + 9 = 14 + x.
Step 2: 3x - x = 14 - 9, so 2x = 5.
Step 3: x = 5/2.
(Answer: x = 5/2.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q3 Solve: 3(2x + 5) = 25 + x

Step 1: 6x + 15 = 25 + x.
Step 2: 5x = 10, x = 2.
(Answer: x = 2.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q4 Solve: 9x - 3 = 3(2x - 8)

Step 1: 9x - 3 = 6x - 24.
Step 2: 9x - 6x = -24 + 3, so 3x = -21.
Step 3: x = -7.
(Answer: x = -7.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q5 Solve: 3(2x - 1) = 5(x - 1)

Step 1: 6x - 3 = 5x - 5.
Step 2: 6x - 5x = -5 + 3, so x = -2.
(Answer: x = -2.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q6 Solve: 2(7x - 6) = 3(1 + 3x)

Step 1: 14x - 12 = 3 + 9x.
Step 2: 5x = 15, x = 3.
(Answer: x = 3.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q7 Solve: (10x - 1)/(2x + 5) = 3

Step 1: Cross-multiply (x not -5/2): 10x - 1 = 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15.
Step 2: 4x = 16, x = 4.
(Answer: x = 4.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q8 Solve: (2x + 1)/(x + 5) = 1

Step 1: 2x + 1 = x + 5 (x not -5).
Step 2: x = 4.
(Answer: x = 4.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q9 Solve: (5x + 3)/(x + 6) = 2

Step 1: 5x + 3 = 2(x + 6) = 2x + 12 (x not -6).
Step 2: 3x = 9, x = 3.
(Answer: x = 3.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q10 Solve: y - 6 + sqrt(y) = 0

Step 1: Transpose: sqrt(y) = 6 - y.
Step 2: Square both sides: y = (6 - y)^2 = y^2 - 12y + 36, so y^2 - 13y + 36 = 0.
Step 3: Factorize: (y - 4)(y - 9) = 0, so y = 4 or y = 9.
Step 4: Check: y = 4 gives 4 - 6 + 2 = 0 (true); y = 9 gives 9 - 6 + 3 = 6 (false, rejected).
Solution set = {4}.
(Answer: y = 4.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q11 Solve: x = 15 - 2 sqrt(x)

Step 1: 2 sqrt(x) = 15 - x.
Step 2: Square: 4x = (15 - x)^2 = x^2 - 30x + 225, so x^2 - 34x + 225 = 0.
Step 3: (x - 9)(x - 25) = 0, so x = 9 or x = 25.
Step 4: Check: x = 9 gives 15 - 2(3) = 9 (true); x = 25 gives 15 - 2(5) = 5, not 25 (rejected).
Solution set = {9}.
(Answer: x = 9.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q12 Solve: m - 13 = sqrt(m + 7)

Step 1: Square both sides: (m - 13)^2 = m + 7, so m^2 - 26m + 169 = m + 7.
Step 2: m^2 - 27m + 162 = 0; factorize: (m - 9)(m - 18) = 0, so m = 9 or m = 18.
Step 3: Check: m = 9 gives L.H.S -4, R.H.S sqrt(16) = 4 (rejected); m = 18 gives 5 = sqrt(25) = 5 (true).
Solution set = {18}.
(Answer: m = 18.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q13 Solve: sqrt(5n + 9) = n - 1

Step 1: Square: 5n + 9 = (n - 1)^2 = n^2 - 2n + 1, so n^2 - 7n - 8 = 0.
Step 2: (n - 8)(n + 1) = 0, so n = 8 or n = -1.
Step 3: Check: n = 8 gives sqrt(49) = 7 = 8 - 1 (true); n = -1 gives sqrt(4) = 2, but n - 1 = -2 (rejected).
Solution set = {8}.
(Answer: n = 8.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q14 Solve: 3 + sqrt(2x - 1) = 0

Step 1: Transpose: sqrt(2x - 1) = -3.
Step 2: A square root is never negative, so this is impossible.
The equation has no (real) solution.
(Answer: No solution.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q15 Solve: sqrt(x + 5) + 7 = 0

Step 1: Transpose: sqrt(x + 5) = -7.
Step 2: A square root is never negative, so this is impossible.
The equation has no (real) solution.
(Answer: No solution.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q16 Solve: sqrt(2x - 1) - sqrt(x - 4) = 2

Step 1: Transpose: sqrt(2x - 1) = 2 + sqrt(x - 4).
Step 2: Square: 2x - 1 = 4 + 4 sqrt(x - 4) + (x - 4), so x - 1 = 4 sqrt(x - 4).
Step 3: Square again: (x - 1)^2 = 16(x - 4), so x^2 - 18x + 65 = 0.
Step 4: (x - 5)(x - 13) = 0, so x = 5 or x = 13.
Step 5: Check: x = 5: sqrt(9) - sqrt(1) = 3 - 1 = 2 (true); x = 13: sqrt(25) - sqrt(9) = 5 - 3 = 2 (true).
Solution set = {5, 13}.
(Answer: x = 5 or x = 13.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q17 Solve: sqrt(x + 1) = 3

Step 1: Square both sides: x + 1 = 9.
Step 2: x = 8.
(Answer: x = 8.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q18 Solve: sqrt(2x - 1) = 5

Step 1: Square both sides: 2x - 1 = 25.
Step 2: 2x = 26, x = 13.
(Answer: x = 13.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q19 Solve: sqrt(x - 1) = 10

Step 1: Square both sides: x - 1 = 100.
Step 2: x = 101.
(Answer: x = 101.)

Exercise 4.1

Q. Q20 Solve: sqrt(3x + 4) = 7

Step 1: Square both sides: 3x + 4 = 49.
Step 2: 3x = 45, x = 15.
(Answer: x = 15.)

mcqs.q: Solve the equation 3x + 20 = 44. What is x?
mcqs.why: Transpose 20: 3x = 44 - 20 = 24. Divide by 3: x = 24/3 = 8. Check: 3(8) + 20 = 44, correct.

mcqs.q: Solve the equation 4x/5 - 3x/4 = 4. What is x?
mcqs.why: The L.C.M of 5 and 4 is 20. Multiply both sides by 20: 16x - 15x = 80, so x = 80. Check: 4(80)/5 - 3(80)/4 = 64 - 60 = 4, correct.

mcqs.q: Solve the equation 3x + 3(x + 1) = 69. What is x?
mcqs.why: Open the bracket: 3x + 3x + 3 = 69, so 6x + 3 = 69. Then 6x = 66 and x = 11. Check: 33 + 3(12) = 69, correct.

mcqs.q: Solve the equation 3(x + 3) = 14 + x. What is x?
mcqs.why: Expand: 3x + 9 = 14 + x. Transpose: 3x - x = 14 - 9, so 2x = 5 and x = 5/2.

mcqs.q: Solve the equation 3(2x + 5) = 25 + x. What is x?
mcqs.why: Expand: 6x + 15 = 25 + x. Transpose: 6x - x = 25 - 15, so 5x = 10 and x = 2.

mcqs.q: Solve the equation 9x - 3 = 3(2x - 8). What is x?
mcqs.why: Expand: 9x - 3 = 6x - 24. Transpose: 9x - 6x = -24 + 3, so 3x = -21 and x = -7.

mcqs.q: Solve the equation 3(2x - 1) = 5(x - 1). What is x?
mcqs.why: Expand: 6x - 3 = 5x - 5. Transpose: 6x - 5x = -5 + 3, so x = -2.

mcqs.q: Solve the equation 2(7x - 6) = 3(1 + 3x). What is x?
mcqs.why: Expand: 14x - 12 = 3 + 9x. Transpose: 14x - 9x = 3 + 12, so 5x = 15 and x = 3.

mcqs.q: Solve the equation (10x - 1)/(2x + 5) = 3. What is x?
mcqs.why: Cross-multiply: 10x - 1 = 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15. Transpose: 10x - 6x = 15 + 1, so 4x = 16 and x = 4.

mcqs.q: Solve the equation (5x + 3)/(x + 6) = 2. What is x?
mcqs.why: Cross-multiply: 5x + 3 = 2(x + 6) = 2x + 12. Transpose: 5x - 2x = 12 - 3, so 3x = 9 and x = 3.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation y - 6 + sqrt(y) = 0. What is the solution set?
mcqs.why: Transpose: sqrt(y) = 6 - y. Square: y = (6 - y)^2 = y^2 - 12y + 36, so y^2 - 13y + 36 = 0 and (y - 4)(y - 9) = 0, giving y = 4 or y = 9. Check: y = 4 gives 4 - 6 + 2 = 0 (true); y = 9 gives 9 - 6 + 3 = 6 (false, rejected). Solution set = {4}.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation x = 15 - 2sqrt(x). What is the solution set?
mcqs.why: Rearrange: 2sqrt(x) = 15 - x. Square: 4x = (15 - x)^2 = x^2 - 30x + 225, so x^2 - 34x + 225 = 0 and (x - 9)(x - 25) = 0, giving x = 9 or x = 25. Check: x = 9 gives 15 - 2(3) = 9 (true); x = 25 gives 15 - 2(5) = 5, not 25 (rejected). Solution set = {9}.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation m - 13 = sqrt(m + 7). What is the solution set?
mcqs.why: Square both sides: (m - 13)^2 = m + 7, so m^2 - 26m + 169 = m + 7 and m^2 - 27m + 162 = 0. Factorize: (m - 9)(m - 18) = 0, giving m = 9 or m = 18. Check: m = 9 gives left side -4 but right side sqrt(16) = 4 (rejected); m = 18 gives 5 = sqrt(25) = 5 (true). Solution set = {18}.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation sqrt(5n + 9) = n - 1. What is the solution set?
mcqs.why: Square: 5n + 9 = (n - 1)^2 = n^2 - 2n + 1, so n^2 - 7n - 8 = 0 and (n - 8)(n + 1) = 0, giving n = 8 or n = -1. Check: n = 8 gives sqrt(49) = 7 = 8 - 1 (true); n = -1 gives sqrt(4) = 2 but n - 1 = -2 (rejected). Solution set = {8}.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation 3 + sqrt(2x - 1) = 0. What is the solution?
mcqs.why: Transpose: sqrt(2x - 1) = -3. A square root is never negative, so this is impossible and the equation has no real solution.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.2 — Absolute Value Equations and Inequalities
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 4.2 of Unit 4 — Linear Equations and Inequalities — complete solved exercises with every step shown.

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q1 Solve: |x| = 9

By the definition of absolute value, x = +9 or x = -9.
Solution set = {-9, 9}. On the number line these are the two points at distance 9 from 0.
(Answer: x = 9 or x = -9.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q2 Solve: |x - 3| = 4

Step 1: x - 3 = +4 or x - 3 = -4.
Step 2: x = 7 or x = -1.
Solution set = {-1, 7}.
(Answer: x = 7 or x = -1.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q3 Solve: |x + 1| = 5

Step 1: x + 1 = +5 or x + 1 = -5.
Step 2: x = 4 or x = -6.
Solution set = {-6, 4}.
(Answer: x = 4 or x = -6.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q4 Solve: |2x - 3| = 5

Step 1: 2x - 3 = +5 or 2x - 3 = -5.
Step 2: 2x = 8 or 2x = -2.
Step 3: x = 4 or x = -1.
Solution set = {-1, 4}.
(Answer: x = 4 or x = -1.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q5 Solve: |3x + 4| = 9

Step 1: 3x + 4 = +9 or 3x + 4 = -9.
Step 2: 3x = 5 or 3x = -13.
Step 3: x = 5/3 or x = -13/3.
Solution set = {-13/3, 5/3}.
(Answer: x = 5/3 or x = -13/3.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q6 Solve the inequality: 3(x - 2) < 2x + 1

Step 1: Expand: 3x - 6 < 2x + 1.
Step 2: Transpose: 3x - 2x < 1 + 6.
Solution: x < 7. Graph: open circle at 7 on the number line, arrow to the left.
(Answer: x < 7.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q7 Solve: 3(x + 5) > 2(x + 2) + 8

Step 1: Expand: 3x + 15 > 2x + 4 + 8 = 2x + 12.
Step 2: 3x - 2x > 12 - 15.
Solution: x > -3. Graph: open circle at -3, arrow to the right.
(Answer: x > -3.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q8 Solve: (1/2)(2 - x) > (1/4)(3 - x) + 1/2

Step 1: Multiply both sides by 4 (positive, sign unchanged): 2(2 - x) > (3 - x) + 2.
Step 2: 4 - 2x > 5 - x.
Step 3: -2x + x > 5 - 4, so -x > 1.
Step 4: Multiply by -1 and reverse the sign: x < -1.
Graph: open circle at -1, arrow to the left.
(Answer: x < -1.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q9 Solve: (x - 2)/4 + 2/3 < (x - 4)/6

Step 1: Multiply by 12 (L.C.M of 4, 3, 6): 3(x - 2) + 8 < 2(x - 4).
Step 2: 3x - 6 + 8 < 2x - 8, so 3x + 2 < 2x - 8.
Step 3: x < -10.
Graph: open circle at -10, arrow to the left.
(Answer: x < -10.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q10 Solve: (3x + 4)/5 - (x + 1)/3 > 1 - (x + 5)/3

Step 1: Multiply by 15: 3(3x + 4) - 5(x + 1) > 15 - 5(x + 5).
Step 2: 9x + 12 - 5x - 5 > 15 - 5x - 25, so 4x + 7 > -5x - 10.
Step 3: 9x > -17.
Solution: x > -17/9. Graph: open circle at -17/9, arrow to the right.
(Answer: x > -17/9.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q11 Solve: (x + 1)/2 - (x + 3)/3 > (x + 1)/4 + 1

Step 1: Multiply by 12: 6(x + 1) - 4(x + 3) > 3(x + 1) + 12.
Step 2: 6x + 6 - 4x - 12 > 3x + 3 + 12, so 2x - 6 > 3x + 15.
Step 3: -6 - 15 > 3x - 2x, so -21 > x.
Solution: x < -21. Graph: open circle at -21, arrow to the left.
(Answer: x < -21.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q12 Solve: (x + 3)/4 - (x + 2)/5 < 1 + (x + 5)/6

Step 1: Multiply by 60: 15(x + 3) - 12(x + 2) < 60 + 10(x + 5).
Step 2: 15x + 45 - 12x - 24 < 60 + 10x + 50, so 3x + 21 < 10x + 110.
Step 3: 21 - 110 < 10x - 3x, so -89 < 7x.
Solution: x > -89/7. Graph: open circle at -89/7, arrow to the right.
(Answer: x > -89/7.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q13 Solve: (1/2)x >= 1 + (1/3)x

Step 1: Multiply by 6: 3x >= 6 + 2x.
Step 2: 3x - 2x >= 6.
Solution: x >= 6. Graph: filled circle at 6, arrow to the right.
(Answer: x >= 6.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q14 Solve: (1/4)(2x + 3) <= 7 - 4x

Step 1: Multiply by 4: 2x + 3 <= 28 - 16x.
Step 2: 2x + 16x <= 28 - 3, so 18x <= 25.
Solution: x <= 25/18. Graph: filled circle at 25/18, arrow to the left.
(Answer: x <= 25/18.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q15 Solve: (4/3)(2x + 3) >= 10 - 4x/3

Step 1: Multiply by 3: 4(2x + 3) >= 30 - 4x.
Step 2: 8x + 12 >= 30 - 4x, so 12x >= 18.
Solution: x >= 3/2. Graph: filled circle at 3/2, arrow to the right.
(Answer: x >= 3/2.)

Exercise 4.2

Q. Q16 Solve: (x - 2)/4 - (x - 5)/6 >= 1/3

Step 1: Multiply by 12: 3(x - 2) - 2(x - 5) >= 4.
Step 2: 3x - 6 - 2x + 10 >= 4, so x + 4 >= 4.
Solution: x >= 0. Graph: filled circle at 0, arrow to the right.
(Answer: x >= 0.)

mcqs.q: Solve the absolute value equation |x| = 9. What is the solution set?
mcqs.why: By the definition of absolute value, |x| = 9 means x is at distance 9 from 0, so x = +9 or x = -9. Solution set = {-9, 9}.

mcqs.q: Solve the absolute value equation |x - 3| = 4. What is the solution set?
mcqs.why: Split into two cases: x - 3 = +4 or x - 3 = -4. Then x = 7 or x = -1. Solution set = {-1, 7}.

mcqs.q: Solve the absolute value equation |x + 1| = 5. What is the solution set?
mcqs.why: Split into two cases: x + 1 = +5 or x + 1 = -5. Then x = 4 or x = -6. Solution set = {-6, 4}.

mcqs.q: Solve the absolute value equation |2x - 3| = 5. What is the solution set?
mcqs.why: Split into two cases: 2x - 3 = +5 or 2x - 3 = -5. Then 2x = 8 or 2x = -2, so x = 4 or x = -1. Solution set = {-1, 4}.

mcqs.q: Solve the absolute value equation |3x + 4| = 9. What is the solution set?
mcqs.why: Split into two cases: 3x + 4 = +9 or 3x + 4 = -9. Then 3x = 5 or 3x = -13, so x = 5/3 or x = -13/3. Solution set = {-13/3, 5/3}.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality where 3(x - 2) is less than 2x + 1. What is the solution?
mcqs.why: Expand: 3x - 6 is less than 2x + 1. Transpose: 3x - 2x is less than 1 + 6, so x is less than 7. On the number line this is an open circle at 7 with an arrow to the left.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality where 3(x + 5) is greater than 2(x + 2) + 8. What is the solution?
mcqs.why: Expand: 3x + 15 is greater than 2x + 4 + 8 = 2x + 12. Transpose: 3x - 2x is greater than 12 - 15, so x is greater than -3. Open circle at -3, arrow to the right.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality (x - 2)/4 + 2/3 is less than (x - 4)/6. What is the solution?
mcqs.why: Multiply by 12, the L.C.M of 4, 3 and 6: 3(x - 2) + 8 is less than 2(x - 4). Expand: 3x + 2 is less than 2x - 8. Transpose: x is less than -10. Open circle at -10, arrow to the left.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality (1/4)(2x + 3) is less than or equal to 7 - 4x. What is the solution?
options: x is less than or equal to 18/25
x is less than or equal to 25/18
x is greater than or equal to 25/18
x is less than or equal to 25
mcqs.why: Multiply by 4: 2x + 3 is less than or equal to 28 - 16x. Transpose: 2x + 16x is less than or equal to 28 - 3, so 18x is less than or equal to 25 and x is less than or equal to 25/18. Filled circle at 25/18, arrow to the left.

mcqs.q: Solve the inequality (x - 2)/4 - (x - 5)/6 is greater than or equal to 1/3. What is the solution?
options: x is greater than or equal to 4
x is less than or equal to 0
x is greater than or equal to 0
x is greater than or equal to -4
mcqs.why: Multiply by 12: 3(x - 2) - 2(x - 5) is greater than or equal to 4. Expand: 3x - 6 - 2x + 10 = x + 4, so x + 4 is greater than or equal to 4 and x is greater than or equal to 0. Filled circle at 0, arrow to the right.
